Image URL: https://images.indianexpress.com/2016/10/agnieszka-radwanska-m.jpg# Radwanska’s China Open Triumph

Agnieszka Radwanska clinched the China Open women’s singles title in Beijing with a commanding 6-4, 6-2 victory over Johanna Konta. The Polish star broke Konta early in the first set, weathered a brief counterbreak, and then sealed the opener before dominating the second set with two more breaks and an ace to serve out the match.

This win marked Radwanska’s 20th career title and her third of the 2016 season, achieved without dropping a set throughout the tournament. The victory also echoed her previous success at the Beijing event in 2011. Konta’s run to the final secured her a spot in the WTA top-10 rankings, making her the first British woman to reach that milestone since 1984.

On court, Radwanska held the ornate gold trophy inscribed “Women’s Singles Champion,” her expression a mix of relief and pride. The bright red and gold of the trophy contrasted with her black athletic attire, capturing the celebratory mood of the final in early October.

Serena Williams clinched her first Western & Southern Open title in Cincinnati on August 17, 2014, overcoming Ana Ivanovic 6-4, 6-1 in a commanding 62-minute performance. After dropping serve in the opening game, Williams rallied with powerful serving—delivering 12 aces—and capitalized on Ivanovic’s unforced errors to seize control of the match.

This victory ended Williams’ long quest for a Cincinnati crown, achieving the milestone on her sixth attempt and improving her finals record to 5-0 for the year. The win also highlighted her resilience, as she recovered from a stiff back and early break to dominate the final. Later that day, Roger Federer added to the tournament’s history by claiming his sixth Cincinnati title.

Venus Williams clinched her 45th career WTA championship at the Dubai Championships with a resounding 6-3, 6-0 victory over France’s Alize Cornet. Entering the tournament on a wild card, Williams extended her perfect record in Dubai to 15 matches and reclaimed the title she previously won in 2009 and 2010. Her win propelled her back into the top 30, rising to No. 29 in the updated rankings.

She lifted the ornate silver trophy—shaped like a traditional Arabic coffee pot—with a beaming smile, celebrating a flawless performance in the final. The image captures the moment of victory and the gleam of the trophy against the darkened stands.

Vera Zvonareva captured the biggest title of her career at the Indian Wells Tennis Garden, overcoming former world No. 1 Ana Ivanovic 7-6 (7-5), 6-2. Battling gusty winds and swirling dust that led to 46 unforced errors from Ivanovic, Zvonareva saved three set points in a marathon first-set tiebreak before seizing control in the second set. 

The fourth-seeded Russian, aged 24, claimed her ninth career trophy and second of the season, following her February win in Pattaya City. Her victory will propel her from No. 6 to No. 5 in the WTA rankings when they are updated.

The victory not only marked a breakthrough on red clay for the Serbian star but also propelled him to the top of the ATP Race standings, edging past Rafael Nadal.

AFP photographer Vincenzo Pinto captured the exact moment Djokovic lifted and kissed the ornate silver trophy, his white shirt contrasting with the gleaming metal. This win represented a significant step toward Djokovic’s goal of becoming world No.1 and set the stage for his upcoming challenge at Roland-Garros.

Image URL: https://a3.espncdn.com/combiner/i?img=%2Fphoto%2F2016%2F1001%2Fr133841_1296x729_16-9.jpg# Kvitová’s Wuhan Open Triumph

Petra Kvitová sealed her 2016 Wuhan Open victory in dominant fashion, defeating Dominika Cibulková 6-1, 6-1 to claim her first title of the year. The Czech left-hander, who previously won the inaugural Wuhan Open in 2014, showcased powerful serving—nine aces—and clinical break-point conversion, winning 17 of the first 18 points in the final.

On court in Wuhan, China, Kvitová embraced the silver singles champion trophy, engraved with “Wuhan Open” and “Wuhan, China,” before planting a celebratory kiss on its sleek surface. Her win propelled her ranking from No. 16 to No. 11 and underscored her affinity for the city and its enthusiastic fans.
